what_its_for: Diflunisal is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to relieve mild to moderate pain, reduce inflammation, and treat symptoms of arthritis such as joint pain, stiffness, and swelling.
how_to_take: Take diflunisal by mouth with a full glass of water (8 ounces). You may take it with food, milk, or antacids to help prevent stomach upset. Do not lie down for at least 10 minutes after taking this medicine. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or break it.
dosing: For pain relief, the usual starting dose is 1000 mg (two 500 mg tablets), followed by 500 mg every 8 to 12 hours as needed. For arthritis, the usual dose is 500 mg to 1000 mg per day, divided into two doses. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different based on your condition and medical history. Do not take more than 1500 mg in one day unless your doctor tells you to.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store diflunisal at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine properly — ask your pharmacist about medication take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking diflunisal, as it increases your risk of stomach bleeding. Do not take aspirin or other NSAIDs (such as ibuprofen or naproxen) at the same time unless your doctor approves. Avoid activities that require alertness if you feel dizzy. Limit salt intake if you have high blood pressure or heart problems. Do not take this medicine if you are allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain or shortness of breath, sudden weakness on one side of the body or slurred speech (signs of a stroke), black or bloody stools, vomit that looks like coffee grounds (signs of stomach bleeding), severe stomach pain, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, skin rash or blistering, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), rapid weight gain or swelling in the legs or ankles, decreased urination, or severe headache. Also call your doctor if your pain or symptoms do not improve or get worse.
when_it_works: Diflunisal usually begins to relieve pain within 1 hour of taking it. The full anti-inflammatory effects for arthritis may take several days to a few weeks of regular use before you notice the most benefit.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with caution, as older adults are at higher risk for stomach bleeding, kidney problems, and heart-related side effects. Use the lowest effective dose. Pregnancy: Do not use diflunisal during the last 3 months (third trimester) of pregnancy, as it can harm the unborn baby. Talk to your doctor before using it earlier in pregnancy. Breastfeeding: Diflunisal passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medicine. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children under 12 have not been established. Kidney or liver disease: Use with caution. Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you closely. Heart disease or high blood pressure: NSAIDs like diflunisal can increase the risk of heart attack or stroke. Talk to your doctor about whether this medicine is safe for you.
